scenes.narration: Who is using all your bandwidth? Interface counters only show the total. NetFlow shows who, and what they're doing.

scenes.heading: Toll booth cameras
scenes.narration: Imagine cameras at a toll booth logging every car. A flow is a stream of packets sharing the same seven fields. Those include addresses, ports, protocol, type of service and interface. Flows are exported after thirty minutes, or fifteen seconds quiet. Records go to a collector over U D P port two zero five five.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. It only records header information. Export uses U D P. The active timeout is thirty minutes.

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.narration: So, to recap. NetFlow shows who talks to whom, not what they say. A flow has seven key fields. Export goes to a collector on U D P two zero five five. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva NetFlow lab.
